properties.name: peristyle court
properties.description: paved court of the peristyle inside the kerb drawn on BCB fig. 166; Ballu gives the open part as 9.50 by 6.25 m (1897b: 229)

properties.name: House of the Hermaphrodite (Maison de l'Hermaphrodite)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1903, pl. XXIII; Boeswillwald, Cagnat and Ballu 1905, fig. 152; Germain 1969, fig. 7
properties.description: peristyle court with twenty-two columns, long central basin and fountain; satellite shows the court and the basin

properties.name: House NW Quarter Row 2 Position 1 (Maison à péristyle nord-ouest quartier, 2e rangée, position 1)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1909: 94-95 (BCTH; offprint pp. 22-23, the report on the 1908 excavations) and 1911a (Sept années): 67-68; the feature as the satellite imagery shows it; round-2 drawing (Oct 6, 2026)
properties.description: the court of the atrium, the open paved area inside its four colonnades, with Ballu's square basin in its south-west corner; the porticoes around it are uneven as he says, the east one the widest (1911a: 67); about 4.7 by 5.2 m

properties.name: House of the Gardens (Maison aux Jardinières)
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1897 I: Pl. XXXVII and fig. 36 (printed p. 224); BCB 1905: fig. 40 (pp. 88-92)

properties.name: atrium
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1926, folding plate (Rapport 1925); round-2 drawing (Oct 1, 2026); Ballu 1916: 178
properties.description: open area of the atrium between the column bases of its north and south porticoes, which Ballu gives as 10.80 m from east to west by 6 m from north to south, with two porticoes of four bays (1916: 178); on his plan the two rows of bases stand about 4.8 m apart, closer than his 6 m

properties.name: paved court
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1926, folding plate (Rapport 1925); round-2 drawing (Oct 1, 2026); Ballu 1916: 176
properties.description: court paved with stone slabs at the south of the house, the cour dallée Ballu describes, opening on its east side onto the portico of five columns along the street and with the door of 1.80 m on its west side into the vestibule (1916: 176), drawn slab by slab on Ballu's plan with two openings in its east wall, and the paving shows as a light patterned surface on the satellite imagery

properties.name: peristyle court
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: the peristyle's open court, Ballu's compluvium of 14.40 by 14.90 m with its central well, the second court of the house, drawn from the west colonnade to the tablinum's west wall, which he says was the court's east side, and between the north and south colonnades (1922: 52)

properties.name: atrium court
properties.plan_source: Ballu, Rapport 1923: 43 (plan), 45-46; Ballu, Rapport 1922: 47-53; Germain 1969: 81, fig. 10; round-2 drawing (Oct 3, 2026), set on the wall lines of the imagery
properties.description: the atrium's open court between its column lines, the first court of the house; Ballu's court of 21.55 by 10.05 m (1922: 48) is the whole atrium with its walks, which is about 21.4 by 9.8 m between the walls as drawn, and the open part is drawn on the columns

properties.name: atrium
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1911a (Sept années): 74, plan of the house, with his description 72-73 (first published in his report on the 1906 excavations, Ballu 1907: 261-262); round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the atrium, paved in limestone, between the tablinum's columns and the east portico, from the north wall down to the three bays onto the central corridor; Ballu gives it as 9.55 by 4.50 m with not one stone of its paving missing (1911a: 72-73), and on the imagery it's a light paved rectangle with the bases' blobs down both sides

properties.name: peristyle court
properties.plan_source: Meunier's unpublished 1938 plan of the house, the fragment Germain reproduces (Germain 1969: 122, fig. 17, right), read from Rebuffat's larger reproduction of it (Rebuffat 1974: pl. 'Thamugadi 12'), with Germain's notes on the floors (1969: 125-127, nos 190-192) and Ballu's plan of the complex (Ballu 1911a: 33) for comparison; round-2 drawing (Oct 4, 2026), set on the walls as the imagery shows them
properties.description: the open court of the peristyle, inside its four colonnades, about 99 m², with the mosaic portico (190) on its west side; the modern path cuts across it diagonally on the imagery

properties.name: atrium (Ballu), the room with the well and the curved wall
properties.plan_source: Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32) for the atrium; Wilson 2001 (fig. 12.08, p. 279) draws the installation in this room; the room as the satellite imagery shows it; round-2 drawing (Oct 13, 2026)
properties.description: the room with the big well and the curved wall, which I take for Ballu's atrium (*bel atrium dallé de pierre, avec grand puits, accompagné, en arrière, d'un mur demi-circulaire*, a fine atrium paved in stone, with a big well, with a semicircular wall behind it, Ballu 1912: 494 (BCTH; offprint p. 32)), since the well with the half-round wall behind it is exactly what the ground shows here and nowhere else in the block, and Wilson draws the installation in this room too; the catch is that Ballu puts his atrium in the east half of the house and this room is in the west half, so either he swapped his east and west for this house or this isn't his atrium, which is why it's uncertain; about 3.8 by 4.4 m inside, which is small for an atrium, and it has no door of its own onto the street; the only door I can see is through the median wall into the east half
